text:
1. Search two permitted source classes for authentic message patterns.
2. Read representative sources and record bounded evidence.
3. Compare structure, language, noise, ambiguity, and artificiality risks.
4. Draft an evidence-linked profile for human review.
I found two source classes and will inspect the documentation example first.

arguments.title: Support chat writing observations
arguments.excerpt: Customers often omit greetings, use fragments such as "charged twice??", include typos, and leave account context implicit.
arguments.observation: Short support requests often use fragments, omit greetings, contain typos, and leave context implicit.
arguments.applicability: Short support-chat and ticket-opening inputs across intent labels.

text: The documentation source is narrow, so I will compare it with a forum source.

arguments.title: Customer forum complaint patterns
arguments.excerpt: Forum complaints can be longer and emotional, but examples still mix fragments, shorthand, irrelevant detail, and unresolved ambiguity.
arguments.observation: Forum inputs broaden the length and emotion range while retaining shorthand, irrelevant detail, and ambiguity.
arguments.applicability: Longer or emotionally charged support inputs and hard or ambiguous cells.

text: I will inspect the accumulated evidence before synthesis.
Both sources support varied completeness and noise; the exact distributions remain uncertain.

claims.statement: Authentic support inputs often omit greetings and use incomplete fragments.
Authentic inputs vary from terse requests to longer emotional complaints and may contain irrelevant detail or unresolved ambiguity.

profile.summary: Generate support inputs with evidence-backed variation in completeness, length, emotion, noise, and ambiguity.

observations: Inputs range from short fragments to longer complaints.
generationInstructions: Vary completeness and length; do not force a greeting or full sentence.
Use ordinary customer vocabulary and occasional shorthand appropriate to the channel.

observations: Typos and irrelevant details occur in authentic requests.
generationInstructions: Apply noise selectively instead of corrupting every row.

observations: Customers may leave account context implicit or leave the issue unresolved.
generationInstructions: For ambiguous cells, omit one useful detail without making the label impossible.

observations: Uniformly polished, complete inputs would conflict with both sources.
generationInstructions: Avoid repeated templates, obligatory greetings, and uniformly polished grammar.
Vary message length, completeness, emotion, and noise independently.
Use source observations abstractly and never reproduce retained excerpts.
caveats: The offline corpus demonstrates the workflow and is not a statistically representative sample.

arguments.summary: An evidence-backed authenticity profile is ready for human review.
